header.running_head: 5. Dhikr and Du'as Taught by the Prophet ﷺ...

blocks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: أَلَا تَسْمَعُ قَوْلَ اللهِ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَكَذلِكَ نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ۞ وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِﷺ: أَيُّمَا مُسْلِمٍ دَعَا بِهَا فِي مَرَضِهِ أَرْبَعِينَ مَرَّةً فَمَاتَ فِي مَرَضِهِ ذلِكَ أُعْطِيَ أَجْرَ شَهِيدٍ وَإِنْ بَرِئئَ بَرِئئَ وَقَدْ غُفِرَ لَهُ جَمِيعُ ذُنُوبِهِ.
blocks.tamil_translation: “Shall I teach you the Ism-ul-A'zam, by means of which, when Du'a is made, Allah accepts it, and by means of which, when anything is asked, Allah gives it? It was with it that Hazrat Yunus (AS) called upon Allah Ta'ala in the three darknesses. It is (لَاإِلهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ) ‘There is none worthy of worship besides You. You are pure from all defects. Indeed, I am the one at fault’,” the Prophet ﷺ said. A man asked Rasulullah ﷺ, “Ya Rasulallah! Is this Kalimah specific to Hazrat Yunus (AS) alone, or is it general for all the believers?” The Prophet ﷺ asked, “Have you not heard the words of Allah Ta'ala: (وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَكَذلِكَ نُنْجِي ) الْمُؤْمِنِينَ” “Just as We saved Hazrat Yunus (AS) from his distress, so shall We save all those who have Iman”?” And he further said: “If a Muslim recites this Du'a forty times while he is ill and dies in that illness, he will be given the reward of a Shaheed. If he recovers from that illness, then along with being cured of it, all his sins will be forgiven.” This hadith is narrated by Hazrat Sa'd ibn Malik (RA).

blocks.text: Explanation:- The three darknesses are the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the fish.
